premises: Some buyers at the margin go without an inspection or use an unlicensed inspector when the fee rises.
buyers.homebuyers.source: From 1 January 2028 every inspector must hold a license.

premises: Some exempt engineers add home inspections, and some buyers accept them.
buyers.homebuyers.source: Exemptions: Licensed professional engineers and architects. About 35 licensed professional engineers inspect homes.

premises: For some part-time inspectors, insurance and the fee exceed their margin, so they stop.
inspectors.licensed.source: the required insurance ($300,000 of errors-and-omissions and general liability cover) about $1,800 a year; the license fee $250 a year. ... a part-timer doing 40, about $50, over 10% of the fee.

premises: Some grandfathered inspectors would otherwise leave for a year or more and return.
inspectors.licensed.source: A license not renewed for 12 months can be restored only by meeting the requirements for a new license.

premises: Exempt engineers and unlicensed practice cannot replace the excluded supply at the old fee (the response is partial).
Engineers' supply cannot expand at unchanged cost in the period.
inspectors.licensed.source: About 210 incumbents (34%) cannot be grandfathered and must train or stop.

premises: The requirements cost some current and would-be inspectors more than they would otherwise spend.
inspectors.licensed.source: For a full-time inspector doing 200 inspections a year, insurance and the license fee add about $10 per inspection; for a part-timer doing 40, about $50.

premises: In the long run, licensed inspectors leave at a lower rate from a smaller stock than inspectors would without the Act, so replacement entry is below the counterfactual flow.
inspectors.licensed.source: About 70 people enter a year and about 50 leave. From 1 July 2027 no one may begin practice without a license.

premises: Inspectors who must train enroll in the first approved courses rather than wait for the 2027 deadline.
inspectors.licensed.source: Training courses are approved from 1 January 2027 and the exam is offered from March 2027. ... from 1 January 2028 every inspector must hold a license.

premises: Agents, schools and the inspectors' association can organize at a cost below their stake.
inspectors.licensed.source: the inspectors' association continuing the campaign for licensing that it had run since 2022.

premises: Some grandfather applicants overstate their inspections, and the Board, checking on paper and acting otherwise only on complaint, misses it.
inspectors.nearline.source: at least 250 fee-paid inspections in those three years, documented by reports. ... Investigation only on a written complaint by a buyer or a licensed agent.

premises: Near-line inspectors win the extra jobs mainly by cutting fees.
inspectors.nearline.source: A near-line inspector at 60 inspections a year, with 180 by mid-2027, needs about 70 more by the end of 2027, more than double their pace.

premises: Total inspections in the window are set by home sales, not raised by the rush.
inspectors.nearline.source: about 61,000 inspections a year. ... Licensed without training or exam on application between 1 July and 31 December 2027, if ... at least 250 fee-paid inspections in those three years.

premises: Some unlicensed practice continues where complaint is least likely.
inspectors.unlicensed.source: The Board shall investigate an alleged violation of this Act only upon a written complaint by a buyer of residential property or by a licensed real-estate agent.

premises: For some part-time inspectors, insurance and the fee exceed their margin, so they stop.
inspectors.unlicensed.source: Unlicensed practice: fine up to $2,500 per inspection. About 80 are part-timers with three years or more but a pace of 40 to 80 inspections a year.

premises: Most Linmouth inspectors serving Aldenmoor do too few jobs there to cover the license's costs.
inspectors.unlicensed.source: The neighboring State of Linmouth has no license; about 12% of Aldenmoor's sales are in the Brask River metro on the border, where about 40 Linmouth inspectors do some Aldenmoor jobs.

premises: Grandfathered inspectors stay in the occupation and their volume does not fall: rivals' exit takes away more inspections than buyers drop.
inspectors.unlicensed.source: Jurisdiction: Inspections of residential property in Aldenmoor, wherever the inspector lives.

premises: Agents, schools and the inspectors' association can organize at a cost below their stake.
agents.realestate.source: A state survey of agents finds that about 70% of buyers hire an inspector their agent recommended.

schools.training.source: Approved training will cost about $3,200 in tuition and about three weeks of time.
